_comment: Canonical list of gota's language templates. The landing page imports this directly, and tests/test_languages.py asserts the rest of the repo agrees (templates/ dirs, README table, run.py, the CI jobs). Adding a language starts here -- see CLAUDE.md.

languages.name: Python
languages.body: The orchestrator's own language and the simplest runner. No build step; run it straight.

languages.name: Rust
languages.body: A single-file rustc build, no Cargo project. Closures plug the op straight in.

languages.name: C
languages.body: The harness is a header plus one translation unit; the op is a function pointer with a void* ctx.

languages.name: C++
languages.body: Header-only: lambdas mean the op inlines into the timing loop, so no function-pointer indirection is needed. C++20, std::span buffer.

languages.name: Go
languages.body: A tiny module with the harness in its own package. go build, then run.

languages.name: Java
languages.body: The op is a functional interface; javac the two files and run Runner.

languages.name: Swift
languages.body: The op is a non-escaping closure over an inout [UInt8]. An @main struct, because swiftc reserves top-level code for main.swift.

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.body: Runs under Node's type stripping (--experimental-strip-types), no transpile step.

languages.name: Haskell
languages.body: Lazy and pure; the op threads a forced accumulator so the work can't be deferred or shared. GHC, stdlib only.
